notes: Closed fixture for the OpenAPI derivation contract (data/contracts/openapi.yaml), executed against the T0419 test-only reference derive() as a separate binding; a later implement task must rebind these rows to its production derivation. Expectations are authored from the structured contract, never computed by the reference. Rows are mutation lists over the shipped control-plane source, whose canonical digest is pinned in source_manifest.

happy.name: baseline-document-shape
happy.why: The shipped source derives the one 3.1.0 document with the pinned top level, info, server, route order and unmapped-code list.

happy.name: baseline-public-and-bearer-security
happy.why: Public operations carry an empty security list; auth-required ones reference bearerAuth.

happy.name: baseline-idempotency-only-on-mutating
happy.why: Every mutating operation references the idempotency header; read-only ones have none.

happy.name: baseline-request-schema-rules
happy.why: Request properties keep source order; required lists required fields in source order; additionalProperties is true; examples are carried.

happy.name: baseline-error-responses-grouped-by-status
happy.why: Contract-fixed statuses 401 and 409 hold their codes in op order; codes with no status stay unmapped, never invented.

happy.name: new-optional-request-field
happy.why: A new optional request field is appended to the properties and left out of required.

happy.name: new-required-request-field
happy.why: A new required request field also lands in required, after the existing ones.

happy.name: write-only-request-field
happy.why: A write-only request field carries writeOnly true in the request schema.

happy.name: new-response-field-is-optional
happy.why: A new optional response field appears in the success schema and not in required.

happy.name: base-path-major-two
happy.why: A major-2 base path becomes the one server URL and the decimal info version.

boundary.name: object-depth-at-ceiling
boundary.why: Objects nested to exactly the depth ceiling of 8 are accepted.

boundary.name: object-depth-over-ceiling
boundary.why: One object level beyond the ceiling of 8 is refused.

boundary.name: fields-per-object-at-ceiling
boundary.why: An object with exactly 256 fields is accepted.

boundary.name: fields-per-object-over-ceiling
boundary.why: An object with 257 fields is refused.

boundary.name: areas-at-ceiling
boundary.why: Exactly 64 areas are accepted.

boundary.name: areas-over-ceiling
boundary.why: 65 areas are refused.

boundary.name: ops-per-area-at-ceiling
boundary.why: Exactly 64 operations in one area are accepted.

boundary.name: ops-per-area-over-ceiling
boundary.why: 65 operations in one area are refused.

boundary.name: example-integer-negative-at-magnitude
boundary.why: The magnitude bound is inclusive on the negative side: -(2^53-1) is accepted.

boundary.name: example-non-ascii-string
boundary.why: A non-ASCII string example is kept as written.

boundary.name: array-example-copied
boundary.why: A string array example is carried into the schema in order.

boundary.name: single-code-closed-enum
boundary.why: A closed enum of one code is accepted when every op and the shape use only it.

boundary.name: base-path-major-ceiling
boundary.why: Major 999 is the largest three-digit major and is accepted.

boundary.name: base-path-major-over-ceiling
boundary.why: Major 1000 has four digits, outside the base path grammar.

boundary.name: base-path-major-zero
boundary.why: Major 0 is outside [1-9][0-9]{0,2}.

boundary.name: base-path-leading-zero-major
boundary.why: A leading zero is outside the major grammar.

boundary.name: example-integer-at-magnitude
boundary.why: An integer example of exactly 2^53-1 is the largest interoperable example.

boundary.name: example-integer-over-magnitude
boundary.why: An integer example of 2^53 is outside the interoperable range.

boundary.name: example-integer-negative-over-magnitude
boundary.why: The magnitude bound is symmetric: -(2^53) is refused.

boundary.name: field-name-at-64-characters
boundary.why: A 64-character field name is the grammar ceiling.

boundary.name: field-name-over-64-characters
boundary.why: A 65-character field name is outside the grammar.

boundary.name: area-name-at-32-characters
boundary.why: A 32-character area name is the grammar ceiling.

boundary.name: area-name-over-32-characters
boundary.why: A 33-character area name is outside the grammar.

boundary.name: route-with-eight-segments
boundary.why: A route of eight segments is the path grammar ceiling.

boundary.name: route-with-nine-segments
boundary.why: A route of nine segments is outside the grammar.

boundary.name: route-segment-at-32-characters
boundary.why: A 32-character route segment is the ceiling.

boundary.name: route-segment-over-32-characters
boundary.why: A 33-character route segment is outside the grammar.

malformed.name: schema-version-one
malformed.why: Only schema_version 2 is read.

malformed.name: schema-version-boolean-true
malformed.why: A boolean is never the integer schema version.

malformed.name: missing-areas
malformed.why: The top level is exactly schema_version, contract, areas.

malformed.name: extra-top-level-key
malformed.why: An extra top-level key breaks the exact key set.

malformed.name: base-path-uppercase
malformed.why: The base path grammar is lowercase.

malformed.name: base-path-trailing-newline
malformed.why: A trailing newline is outside the anchored grammar.

malformed.name: base-path-not-a-string
malformed.why: The base path must be a string.

malformed.name: get-op-with-request-fields
malformed.why: A GET operation must declare no request fields.

malformed.name: unknown-method
malformed.why: Only GET and POST are declared methods.

malformed.name: unknown-auth-value
malformed.why: auth is public or required.

malformed.name: public-op-missing-from-public-list
malformed.why: An op is public exactly when its auth is public and it is listed.

malformed.name: required-op-listed-public
malformed.why: An auth-required op listed as public breaks the public rule.

malformed.name: read-only-flag-without-list-entry
malformed.why: mutating false and the read-only list must agree both ways.

malformed.name: error-code-outside-closed-enum
malformed.why: An op error code outside the closed enum is malformed.

malformed.name: duplicate-error-code-in-op
malformed.why: An op lists distinct error codes.

malformed.name: example-bool-for-integer
malformed.why: A boolean is never an integer example.

malformed.name: example-string-for-integer
malformed.why: An example must have the declared type.

malformed.name: example-lone-surrogate
malformed.why: A string example must be UTF-8 encodable, with no lone surrogate.

malformed.name: array-example-with-a-bad-item
malformed.why: Every item of an array example must have the declared item type.

malformed.name: array-example-first-item-bad
malformed.why: One valid later item does not excuse an invalid first item.

malformed.name: field-without-type
malformed.why: A field descriptor must declare its type.

malformed.name: field-without-required
malformed.why: A field descriptor must declare required.

malformed.name: closed-enum-empty
malformed.why: The closed error enum must list at least one code.

malformed.name: unknown-field-key
malformed.why: A field descriptor carries only the declared keys.

malformed.name: unknown-field-type
malformed.why: Field types are a closed set.

malformed.name: array-without-items
malformed.why: Only arrays carry items and an array must declare them.

malformed.name: items-on-a-string-field
malformed.why: Only arrays have items.

malformed.name: object-field-with-example
malformed.why: An object field has fields and no example.

malformed.name: write-only-in-a-response
malformed.why: A write-only field may appear only in request schemas.

malformed.name: chess-token-field-name
malformed.why: No derived property name contains a chess content token.

malformed.name: chess-token-nested-field-name
malformed.why: The chess token rule holds at every depth.

malformed.name: duplicate-route
malformed.why: Two operations may not share a method and path.

malformed.name: op-with-unknown-key
malformed.why: An operation carries exactly the declared keys.

malformed.name: hostile-source-is-a-list
malformed.why: The source must be a mapping.

rollback.name: refusal-then-baseline-is-identical
rollback.why: A refused derivation leaves no state: deriving the shipped source afterwards gives the pinned golden bytes.

rollback.name: accept-then-refusal-then-accept
rollback.why: An accepted derivation, a refusal and another accepted derivation do not disturb one another.

rollback.name: late-failure-returns-no-partial-document
rollback.why: The last operation is malformed: the whole derivation is refused, never a partial document.
